findings.reason: the section must either name an imas-ink extension for multi-panel/line-styled geometry (as §4 does) or admit the script does the compositing, and §2 currently is its own contradiction.
findings.text: §2 requires "OP1 and OP2 side by side on one shared viewport" and, for the second figure, "overlays the two phases' first wall and vessel contours on one panel … telling the phases apart by line style alone", while declaring the script "draws no element itself and holds no colour, label or style constant". `imas_ink.figures.geometry_figure_mpl` (imas_ink/figures.py:138) creates its own figure and axes from `plt.subplots(...)`, takes no `ax` argument, and exposes no per-series or per-phase linestyle control; `extract_geometry` returns a single `MachineGeometry` with no multi-phase composition. So neither "side by side on one shared viewport" nor "apart by line style alone" can be produced through the named API without the script composing axes and setting linestyles itself — the exact styling §2 promises not to do — or without extending imas-ink. §2 waits on the machine-map wall rewrite and §4 only, so it does not treat the compositing ability as an imas-ink addition the way §4 treats the vessel.

findings.reason: the plan should name the catalogue owner for phase addressing (or place the phase/IDS reader beside description_reader.py) rather than route the store join through an engine `open` that neither yields a directory nor removes the catalogue dependency.
findings.text: §2 takes "each phase directory from `NetCDFTransformEngine.open`". That method (imas_ambix/data/transform_engine.py:361) does not return a directory: it returns a `_NetCDFStoreArrays` resolved as `root / machine_map.name`, so a caller still needs the store root first. The catalogue already owns that resolution — `MachineMapCatalog.description_store_root_path` (imas_ambix/data/machine_map.py:1006) and `resolve_description_store_root` (machine_map.py:118) — and `imas_ambix/data/description_reader.py` owns the catalogue→store→description path (`_resolve_store_addressing`, `read_geometry_table`) used by `gs/grounding.py`, `spine_bench/runner.py` and `tokenizer/signal_hf_encode.py`. The retired §1 script (scripts/figures_jt60sa_geometry.py:253) already resolved the phase as `catalog.description_store_root_path() / machine_map.name`; §2 introduces a second, lower-level path to the same join. No other instance of this defect exists in the plan — §3's `read_channel` reuses `channel_path`/`channel_time_path`/`UNIT_ATTR` and §4 reuses `VesselShell` rather than forking them.

duplicate_owner-1.reason: plan v31 §2 takes the store root from the catalogue's description_store_root_path() and the phase directory from the store NetCDFTransformEngine.open returns on that root and map

thin_wrapper-1.reason: plan v31 §2 renders through an ax argument and a reference wall_linestyle that imas-ink's geometry-figure-vessel-units plan adds as its §2, naming the imas-ink extension the figures need

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §4 extends one deep existing owner (`extract_vessel_shells` gains the `outline_inner`/`outline_outer` reading and feeds a typed `MachineGeometry` field) rather than spreading the vessel across new wrappers; §2 and §3 add deliberately thin orchestration scripts over imas-ink and say so. No new module hides substantial behaviour behind many small wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §2 re-derives the phase/store addressing through `NetCDFTransformEngine.open` instead of the catalogue owner `MachineMapCatalog.description_store_root_path` (imas_ambix/data/machine_map.py:1006), the mechanism the retired §2's duties are replacing.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §3 names its one public addition (`read_channel`) and states it "retires nothing"; §4 names its one public addition (`MachineGeometry.vessel`) and states why nothing can be retired ("the 2D geometry has no vessel representation today"); §2's new script is the replacement §1b retires. Every adding section accounts for its surface in its own text.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan searched the codebases it extends and cites the mechanisms: §3 names `imas_ambix/data/eddb.py` as the cache owner it adds the read beside and `ZarrTransformEngine.read` (transform_engine.py:142) as the engine it declines because it returns a bare array; §4 names the existing vessel owner `extract_vessel_shells` (imas_ink/three_d/walls.py:151) and reuses its `VesselShell` type (imas_ink/three_d/walls.py:42). I confirmed no reader of the EDDB cache exists (`channel_path`/`channel_time_path` are called only by `write_channel`/`_channel_present` and tests) and no caller of `extract_geometry`/`geometry_figure_mpl` exists in ambix, so §3's reader and §2's figure are genuine gaps, not rebuilds.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §2 adds thin scripts over `imas_ink.figures.geometry_figure_mpl` and asserts they "draw no element" and "hold no colour, label or style constant", but imas-ink's API cannot express the two figures §2 requires (multi-panel composition and per-phase line-style differentiation), and §2 does not name that as an imas-ink extension the way §4 does for the vessel.
